slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel like
cheating when you meet her parents
Ask her before you go what her parents love. Gardening, football, old films, their dog. Then ask them about it. "I heard you grow your own tomatoes?" Now they're talking, and you're doing great.
Bring something small. Flowers for her mum, a dessert for the table, a good bottle if they drink. Don't overthink it. Arriving with something in your hands says you were raised right.
Offer to help, and mean it. Carry plates, dry dishes, set the table. "Can I give you a hand?" Even if they say no, they'll remember you asked. Then ask again after dinner.
Put your phone away for the whole visit. Not on the table, not in your hand. Her parents are watching how you pay attention, and this is the easiest way to pass the test without saying a word.
Try this for 30 days before the visit: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Parents love a guy who can talk about more than his job. You'll have real things to share at the table.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days before the visit: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Parents love a guy who can talk about more than his job. You'll have real things to share.

slides.texte_overlay: Laugh at her dad's jokes, but don't overdo it. Smile, react naturally, maybe ask "Is that a true story?" Showing you enjoy their company works better than trying too hard to be the funny guy.
Say thank you properly before you leave. "Thanks so much for having me, dinner was amazing." Then text her later to pass on another thank you. Parents remember the guy who said it twice.
